q.instruction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
q.passage: Alcohol has been a big part of ⓐ<u>college</u> life . . . ⓑ<u>drink</u> hard. ⓒ<u>unshared</u> context But a new kind of drinking known as “ⓓ<u>binge</u>” drinking is spreading . . . kills and injures not just drinkers but those around them. problem We may not be able to stop bingeing entirely, but we must try to ­control its worst costs by educating students in how to manage its risks. solution/main point/claim Part 1: Establishing a Shared Context Most pieces of writing open with a shared context, as does (1b): Alcohol has been a big part of college life for hundreds of years. From football weekends to fraternity parties, college students drink and often drink hard. shared context But a new kind of drinking ⓔ<u>known</u> as “binge” . . .
